messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick update: new remote-location and WFH benefits policy is live. Highlights: monthly internet stipend $120 (prorated first month), one-time home office setup reimbursement up to $400 (submit receipts within 45 days), and revised relocation intake requiring a tax & payroll pre-check for any permanent address change. Please read the checklist and file the form before you move. :spiral_note_pad:

Liam (Recruiter): Nice. For offers, do we now include a relocation clause or wait for People Ops approval first?

Maya (People Ops): Good call. If candidate requests relocation as a condition, route to People Ops before offer acceptance. We need to confirm tax implications and benefits eligibility. Use the "remote-relocate" checkbox on the offer template.

Sato (Eng Manager): A couple of practical Qs: 1) If someone moves within the same state but to a different city, any payroll action? 2) Does contractor -> employee status affect stipend?

Maya (People Ops): 1) In-state moves usually only need address update in payroll/benefits; no nexus review. 2) Stipends are for employees only; contractors should get vendor/contract terms via Procurement. We'll add a note to the contractor policy.

Priya (IC): I'm thinking of moving from NY to NJ in August. What's the timeline? I don't want a payroll gap.

Maya (People Ops): Please submit the relocation intake form at least 30 days before your effective move date. Payroll needs 7 business days to change tax withholding, benefits ops need up to 15 business days to adjust coverage. If you want a relocation reimbursement, attach receipts and manager approval.

Priya (IC): Cool. What about taxable vs non-taxable reimbursements? We got a lump sum offer in another company and it was taxed.

GlobalTax: FYI: reimbursements under an accountable plan (receipts + business purpose + timely reporting) can be non-taxable. Flat lump-sum payments are usually taxable and may require gross-up if company agrees. For cross-border moves, there may be payroll and employer-withholding obligations in the destination country.

Liam (Recruiter): International hires question: if we hire remote in UK, do we need to hire via local entity or EOR?

GlobalTax: Depends on headcount and activity. For single hires, EOR (Employer of Record) is typical. If multiple hires and ongoing business, entity setup may be required. People Ops + Finance will advise on a case-by-case basis.

Maya (People Ops): Filing link + short checklist:
```
Form: https://redwoodincorp.internal/hr/remote-relocate
Checklist:
- new address + effective date
- anticipated stipend or relocation reimbursement (itemized)
- manager approval email or slack thread link
- receipts for accountable-plan reimbursement
- hire vs contractor status noted
```

Sato (Eng Manager): Any special rules for states with reciprocal tax agreements (e.g., PA/NJ)?

GlobalTax: Reciprocal agreements matter for withholding but not for employer-side unemployment or nexus analysis. We'll handle withholding changes but will flag anything unusual.

Maya (People Ops): Note for managers: if offering a relocation package > $7,500, loop in Finance for tax gross-up planning. Also, for hiring cases where the candidate wants to permanently work from another country, do not finalize until People Ops signs off.

Priya (IC): Submitted intake form with tentative move date 2024-08-12 and list of expected costs.

Payroll-Bot: automated: Payroll task created PT-4478 to update withholding and address. Estimated processing: 5 business days after form verification.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you have urgent moves or edge cases (long-term travel, sabbatical, or temporary assignment), DM People Ops. We'll post the full policy doc to the handbook this afternoon. :white_check_mark:
